metadata.title: Social Security Death Index: Uncovering Hidden Clues | Ancestry
metadata.author: Ancestry
metadata.shortDescription:
It's easy to find an entry in the Social Security Death Index. But have you uncovered the "Last Benefit/Last Resident" clues?

Start Your Journey Today:
http://www.ancestry.com/s89715/t38352/rd.ashx

Subscribe: http://www.youtube.com/channel/UCsc0AQkAh_2cQmxqwD6VWRw?sub_confirmation=1

About Ancestry:
Bringing together science and self-discovery, Ancestry helps everyone, everywhere discover the story of what led to them. Our sophisticated engineering and technology harnesses family history and consumer genomics, combining billions of rich historical records and millions of family trees to over 10 million and counting to provide people with deeply meaningful insights about who they are and where they come from. 
We’ve pioneered and defined this category, developing new innovations and technologies that have reinvented how people make family history discoveries. And these discoveries can give everyone a greater sense of identity, relatedness, and their place in the world.

you'll find the name birth date death
date place and year the social security
number was issued but what you may have
missed is in the last residence or last
benefit let's start with the most basic
Social Security death index entry this
one for DW Gibson shows us his social
security number his birth date his death
date and that he applied for a social
security number in North Carolina in
1963 there is no last benefit or last
residence information so we know nothing
more than the basic
information some entries will have a

Carolina now let's look at Martha
Gibson's father Gilbert M gespi you'll
notice that he has a last residence
instead of a last benefit this means
that when he died no one else was
eligible to collect benefits from his
Social Security count because his wife
had died before him and he had no
dependent children so we know that he
died after his
wife so remember if there is a last
benefit either a surviving spouse or
dependent child was eligible to receive
the deceased benefits if there's a less
residents this is more likely the last
resident the Social Security
Administration knew about when paying
that person's
benefits also if there is no last

that someone is still collecting

had no
dependence a couple more things
ancestry.com does not show the social

the
left this page walks you through the

write a letter to the Social Security
Administration to get a copy of the
ss5 so when you look at this Social
Security death index make sure that you
record and understand all five pieces
that you might be looking at name birth
date death date place in year the social
security number was issued and whether
you see a less residence or less benefit
and you understand the difference
between the two thanks for listening
happy searching
